title: Vietnam Temple of Literature: Tickets, Hours and Tips
description: Temple of Literature in Hanoi: official day and night-tour ticket prices, opening hours, the route through its courtyards, dress rules and the quietest times.
h1: Vietnam's Temple of Literature: tickets, hours and how to plan a visit
intro: Vietnam's Temple of Literature (Văn Miếu – Quốc Tử Giám) is a Confucian temple in Hanoi founded in 1070. It is open daily from 8:00 to 17:00, and the entrance is at 58 Quốc Tử Giám Street. You buy a day ticket at the counter, or online if you have a Vietnamese bank app, and children under 16 get in free. A separate night tour runs on Wednesday, Saturday and Sunday evenings. Most visitors need 60 to 90 minutes for the main courtyards.
keyPoints: The official site lists three day-ticket tiers as of November 2026: standard {{vnd:70000}}, priority {{vnd:35000}} and free for children under 16.
The priority rate is for students of Vietnamese schools with a student card, people aged 60 and over and some people with disabilities. Bring proof.
Daytime opening is 8:00 to 17:00 every day, according to vanmieu.gov.vn as of November 2026. The night tour runs on Wednesday, Saturday and Sunday evenings and needs its own ticket.
Go on a weekday between 8:00 and 9:30 to avoid tour groups and school trips. Avoid the 11:00 to 14:00 heat.
Cover your shoulders and knees, and do not touch the 82 doctoral steles. Their turtles are protected relics, not something to rub for luck.

sections.title: Where is the Temple of Literature in Vietnam?

blocks.text: The Temple of Literature is in central Hanoi, about 2 to 3 km west of Hoan Kiem Lake. Its main entrance is at **58 Quốc Tử Giám Street**. In Vietnamese it is Văn Miếu – Quốc Tử Giám: Văn Miếu is the temple to Confucius, and Quốc Tử Giám is the Imperial Academy built beside it.

The site is run by Hanoi's city authorities, and its official website is [vanmieu.gov.vn](https://vanmieu.gov.vn/en). The site's history page says Văn Miếu was built in 1070 under King Lý Thánh Tông. King Lý Nhân Tông founded Quốc Tử Giám in 1076. VnExpress calls the academy the country's first national university.

Many people still give the address as Dong Da district. Since July 2025, official addresses use new ward names, and the official site now gives the location as Văn Miếu – Quốc Tử Giám Ward, Hanoi. The site has two exits: one at 19–21 Văn Miếu Street, and the Vườn Giám garden exit opposite 40 Tôn Đức Thắng Street.

blocks.title: Hanoi, not Ho Chi Minh City
blocks.text: The Temple of Literature is in Hanoi, not Ho Chi Minh City. If you are weighing up the two cities for a longer stay, start with [Vietnam cities compared](/guides/vietnam-cities-compared) or [Hanoi vs Ho Chi Minh City for teachers](/teach-in-vietnam/hanoi-vs-ho-chi-minh-city-for-teachers).

sections.title: How much are Temple of Literature tickets?

blocks.text: A standard day ticket costs {{vnd:70000}} and a priority ticket costs {{vnd:35000}}. Children under 16 get in free. These are the prices on the [official visitor information page](https://vanmieu.gov.vn/introduction/visitor-information) as of November 2026.

blocks.caption: Temple of Literature day tickets, from vanmieu.gov.vn, checked 27 November 2026
rows: Students of Vietnamese schools; people aged 60 and over; people with severe disabilities; people covered by cultural benefit policies
Student card, citizen ID (CCCD) or the documents the rules require
Children under 16; people with especially severe disabilities

blocks.text: Do foreign students and seniors get the priority rate?

The official wording links the student rate to students of **Vietnamese schools** with a student card, and the senior rate to people aged 60 and over with a CCCD, which is the Vietnamese citizen ID. A foreign student card or a passport is not mentioned as proof. Ask at the ticket and information counter before you count on the discount.
How do you pay at the ticket counter?

The official site sells day tickets online at vanmieu.gov.vn/en/tickets: you pay by QR code from a Vietnamese bank or e-wallet app, and the gate QR is emailed to you, valid for 30 days. International payment is "coming soon", so without a Vietnamese bank app, buy at the counter. The site does not say which payment methods the counter accepts. A Vietnam Tourism guide updated in October 2026 says the counter takes cash only and that there is no ATM on site. Carry small notes.
VnExpress reported in November 2024 that a foreign-language audio guide cost an extra {{vnd:100000}}. That figure has not been confirmed since, so check it at the counter.

sections.title: When is the Temple of Literature open, and when should you go?

blocks.text: The Temple of Literature is open every day from 8:00 to 17:00, according to vanmieu.gov.vn as of November 2026. The quietest time is a weekday between 8:00 and 9:30, before the tour groups arrive.

Other sources give different hours. In November 2024, VnExpress listed summer hours of 7:30 to 17:30 (15 April to 15 October) and winter hours of 8:00 to 17:00. The October 2026 Vietnam Tourism guide gives 8:00 to 17:00 with last entry at 16:30. Plan around the official hours and arrive by 16:30.

blocks.caption: Crowds and conditions by time of day, from Vietnam Tourism (October 2026)
rows: Quietest; best for photographing the stele garden
Hottest part of the day, with little shade on the paths
The most comfortable season; the days around Tet are busy

blocks.title: Tet closures
blocks.text: Vietnam Tourism says the site closes on some public holidays, including several days around Tet. The official site publishes no holiday calendar. If you plan to go in late January or February, check vanmieu.gov.vn or ask your hotel first.

sections.title: What is the Van Mieu night tour and how do you book it?

blocks.text: The night tour is a separate evening programme with its own ticket. It runs on Wednesday, Saturday and Sunday evenings and includes a 3D projection-mapping show called "Tinh hoa đạo học". The Vietnamese pages of the official site give the hours as 18:30 to 22:00, while the English home page says 18:00 to 22:00. Confirm the show time when you book.

The [official night tour page](https://vanmieu.gov.vn/experience/night-tour) lists more than the show: meeting a calligrapher, the doctoral stele of 1484, and printing a Khuê Văn Các woodblock onto dó paper. Ticket types depend on height, not age.

blocks.caption: Night tour prices, from vanmieu.gov.vn, checked 27 November 2026

blocks.text: Children under 1.0 m tall go in free. The official page does not say what the second show in the two-show package is, how long the tour lasts or which languages are used. Ask when you book.

items.title: Open the booking page
items.text: Go to the night tour section of vanmieu.gov.vn and choose the programme.

items.title: Pick a date and show time
items.text: The booking flow shows the dates that are available. They are not published as a list.

items.title: Choose the tickets
items.text: Enter the number of adult and child tickets. Use the height bands above, not age.

items.title: Pay online
items.text: Payment goes through OnePay. The tickets are then sent to your email, so use an address and phone that work in Vietnam (see the [SIM and eSIM guide](/esim-vietnam-guide)).

items.title: Read the refund policy before you pay
items.text: The site links to a separate cancellation and refund policy. Read it if your plans might change.

sections.title: What is there to see inside the Temple of Literature?

blocks.text: The site is a series of walled courtyards that you walk through in a straight line. The highlights are the Khuê Văn Các pavilion, the garden of 82 doctoral steles around the Thiên Quang well, the Đại Thành sanctuary and the Thái Học academy buildings. This is the route on the official site map.

items: **Phương Đình and Văn Lake**, outside the gate, with the Hạ Mã stele, where riders once had to dismount.
**Văn Miếu gate**, then **Đại Trung gate** (Great Middle Gate), into the first courtyards.
**Khuê Văn Các**, the pavilion of the constellation of literature. The Vietnam Tourism guide says it was built in 1805 and is a symbol of Hanoi.

**The stele garden around the Thiên Quang well.** According to the Viet Nam Government Portal, 82 steles on stone turtles record 1,304 doctoral laureates of royal exams held from 1442 to 1779. The steles were added to UNESCO's Memory of the World Register on 26 May 2011.
**Đại Thành gate and the Đại Thành sanctuary**, a working place of worship with altars to Confucius and his disciples.
**Thái Học gate and the Thái Học building**, on the site of the old Imperial Academy, with the drum tower and bell tower. The official history says work on the Thái Học compound began in 1999.
**The exit and the octagonal house in Vườn Giám garden**, where you come out onto Tôn Đức Thắng Street.

blocks.text: The official site also lists heritage education sessions and calligraphy practice. Its English home page marks both as free entry, but it publishes no session times, so ask at the information counter when you arrive. The site also has a bookshop, a souvenir shop and toilets.

sections.title: What should you wear, and what are the rules on site?

blocks.text: Dress modestly, because the temple is still a place of worship. The official rules ask for polite dress in the worship areas and quiet in the solemn spaces. The October 2026 Vietnam Tourism guide says staff turn away tank tops, crop tops, shorts above mid-thigh and skirts above the knee.

items: Do not touch, write on or draw on the steles, the turtles or the buildings. The official rules make visitors liable for any damage.
Keep off the grass, and do not pick flowers or break branches.
No smoking anywhere on the grounds.
VnExpress (November 2024) adds that food and drink are not allowed inside, and that you should light only one incense stick, in the offering areas provided.
Vietnam Tourism asks visitors not to photograph the main altar in the Đại Thành sanctuary and to take hats off inside the sanctuaries.

blocks.title: Bring a cover-up
blocks.text: Carry a light shirt or scarf in your bag. Vietnam Tourism says the cover-ups sold outside the gate are poor quality, and Hanoi's summer heat makes long sleeves the last thing you want to wear on the walk there.

sections.title: How do you get to the Temple of Literature?

blocks.text: Most visitors walk from Hoan Kiem Lake, which takes about 15 minutes according to VnExpress, or take a taxi or Grab to 58 Quốc Tử Giám Street. City buses and Metro Line 2A also stop nearby.

blocks.caption: Ways to get there, from the official site map (checked 27 November 2026) and VnExpress (November 2024)
rows: Stop at 58 Quốc Tử Giám Street (official site)
Stop opposite 40 Tôn Đức Thắng Street, by the Vườn Giám exit (official site)
Cát Linh station, about 700 m away (VnExpress, 2024)
Parking along Văn Miếu Street (official site)

blocks.text: If you are coming from Ho Chi Minh City, the temple is easy to fit into a short Hanoi trip. For travel tickets and attractions on eno.vn, browse [Tickets and travel](/c/tickets-travel).

sections.title: What this guide does not cover

items: Holiday closures and special event days: the official site publishes no calendar, so check vanmieu.gov.vn or the counter before Tet and national holidays.
Private guided tours and their prices: these come from tour operators, not the site, and prices vary.
Other Hanoi sights and where to stay in Hanoi: for living in the city, see [apartments for rent in Tay Ho](/guides/apartment-for-rent-in-tay-ho).
A full history of Vietnam's royal examinations: the [official site history](https://vanmieu.gov.vn/en/introduction/site-history) has the timeline.

faqs.q: What is the Temple of Literature in Vietnam?
faqs.a: The Temple of Literature in Vietnam, called Văn Miếu – Quốc Tử Giám in Vietnamese, is a Confucian temple in Hanoi built in 1070 under King Lý Thánh Tông. In 1076 the Imperial Academy was founded beside it, which VnExpress calls the country's first national university. The temple's 82 doctoral steles record royal exams held from 1442 to 1779 and are on UNESCO's Memory of the World Register.

faqs.q: How much is the Temple of Literature ticket in Vietnam?
faqs.a: The Temple of Literature has three day-ticket tiers, according to the official site vanmieu.gov.vn as of November 2026. There is a standard adult ticket, a priority ticket at half the standard price, and free entry for children under 16. The priority ticket is for students of Vietnamese schools, people aged 60 and over and some people with disabilities. The night tour has separate prices, listed in the ticket sections of this guide.

faqs.q: What time does the Temple of Literature open?
faqs.a: The Temple of Literature in Hanoi is open every day from 8:00 to 17:00, according to the official site vanmieu.gov.vn as of November 2026. One October 2026 travel guide gives last entry as 16:30, so arrive before then. A separate ticketed night tour runs on Wednesday, Saturday and Sunday evenings. Some older sources list longer summer hours, so check the official site if you plan an early start.

faqs.q: Where is the Temple of Literature in Vietnam?
faqs.a: The Temple of Literature is in central Hanoi, at 58 Quốc Tử Giám Street, about 2 to 3 km west of Hoan Kiem Lake. Since July 2025 its official address has been in Văn Miếu – Quốc Tử Giám Ward, although many people still say Dong Da district. Bus 38 stops at the entrance, and Cát Linh station on Metro Line 2A is about 700 m away.

faqs.q: Can you pay by card at the Temple of Literature?
faqs.a: The official Temple of Literature visitor page does not say which payment methods the day-ticket counter accepts. A Vietnam Tourism guide updated in October 2026 says the counter takes cash only and that there is no ATM on site, so carry small notes. Night tour tickets are different: they are booked and paid for online on vanmieu.gov.vn through OnePay, and the tickets are sent by email.

faqs.q: What should you wear to the Temple of Literature in Vietnam?
faqs.a: Wear clothes that cover your shoulders and knees to the Temple of Literature, because it is still a place of worship. The official rules ask for polite dress in the worship areas. A Vietnam Tourism guide from October 2026 says staff turn away tank tops, crop tops, shorts above mid-thigh and skirts above the knee. Bring a light cover-up, as the ones sold outside the gate are poor quality.

faqs.q: When does the Temple of Literature night tour run?
faqs.a: The Temple of Literature night tour runs on Wednesday, Saturday and Sunday evenings, according to the official site vanmieu.gov.vn as of November 2026. The Vietnamese pages give 18:30 to 22:00 and the English home page gives 18:00 to 22:00, so confirm the show time when you book. The tour includes a 3D projection-mapping show and calligraphy, and ticket types depend on height rather than age.

faqs.q: How long do you need at the Temple of Literature?
faqs.a: Most visitors need 60 to 90 minutes to see the main courtyards of the Temple of Literature in Hanoi, according to a Vietnam Tourism guide from October 2026. That covers Khuê Văn Các, the doctoral stele garden, the Đại Thành sanctuary and the Thái Học buildings. Go on a weekday between 8:00 and 9:30 for the quietest visit, before tour groups and school trips arrive.
